questions.q: Two capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ are connected in parallel to a battery. Charge-time graph is shown below for the two capacitors. The energy stored with them are $U_1$ and $U_2$, respectively. Which of the given statements is true?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a capacitor at steady state
$q=C V \text { and } U=\frac{1}{2} C V^2$

Since $C_1$ and $C_2$ are connected in parallel, $V_1=V_2$.
Also from graph $q_1 \lt  q_2\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad C_1 V_1 \lt  C_2 V_2 \\
& \text { i.e. } C_1 \lt  C_2 \text { or } C_2 \gt C_1 \\
& \qquad \frac{U_1}{U_2}=\frac{C_1 V_1^2}{C_2 V_2^2}=\frac{C_1}{C_2} \lt  1
\end{aligned}$
or $U_1 \lt  U_2$ or $U_2 \gt U_1$

∴ E =q12ε0A-q22ε0A=q1-q22ε0A   ...1

For parallel plate capacitor C = ε0Ad   ...2

From above two equations 

E=q1-q22Cd   ...3 

∵ Relation between intensity of field E and potential difference V between the plates is

From equation 3 and 4

V = q1-q22C

questions.q: A capacitor, $C_1=6 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ is charged to a potential difference of $\mathrm{V}_0=5 \mathrm{~V}$ using a 5 V battery. The battery is removed and another capacitor, $\mathrm{C}_2=12 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ is inserted in place of the battery. When the switch 'S' is closed, the charge flows between the capacitors for some time until equilibrium condition is reached. What are the charges $\left(q_1\right.$ and $\left.q_2\right)$ on the capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ when equilibrium condition is reached.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{q}_1^{\prime}=6 \times 5=30 \mu \mathrm{C}$ Finally
$\begin{aligned} & 6 \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{C}}+12 \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{c}}=30+0 \\ & 18 \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{C}}=30 \\ & \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{30}{18}=\frac{5}{3} \mathrm{Volt} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{q}_1=\frac{6 \times 5}{3}=10 \mu \mathrm{C} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{q}_2=\frac{12 \times 5}{3}=20 \mu \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Consider a parallel plate capacitor of area A (of each plate) and separation 'd' between the plates. If $E$ is the electric field and $\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space between the plates, then potential energy stored in the capacitor is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know energy density
$\rho_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0 E^2$
So potential energy $=\rho_{a v} \times$ Volume
$\Rightarrow \text { P.E. }=\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0 E^2 A d$
